newsitem.title: MEXICO: Senior U.S. officials pledge commitment to Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Senior U.S. officials pledge commitment to Mexico.

text.p: U.S. anti-drugs chief Gen. Barry McCaffrey and U.S. Acting National Security Adviser Samuel "Sandy" Berger made a surprise trip to Mexico City on Wednesday to express Washington's commitment to stronger ties with Mexico in all spheres including the war on drugs.

The two officials, accompanied by (U.S.) President (Bill) Clinton's special adviser for Latin America Thomas "Mack" McClarty, told reporters they had met President Ernesto Zedillo and passed on Clinton's wish to strengthen the two countries' relationship.

"We have come here today at the request of President Clinton to meet with our colleagues and with President Zedillo to express President Clinton's commitment to strengthening the U.S.-Mexico relationship, based on mutual respect and shared interests, including in our common fight against drugs," Berger told reporters.
Berger took no questions after reading the statement at Zedillo's official residence of Los Pinos.
He said the high-level delegation had also come to Mexico to help fine-tune details of Clinton's scheduled visit to Mexico on April 11-12.
Washington on Friday renewed its annual "certification" that Mexico is an ally in its anti-narcotics efforts, despite opposition from critics of Mexican drug corruption.
